STATUTORY POLICY MANUAL, DELEGATION OF POWERS FOR DEFENCE LAND TRANSFERS, AND STANDING OPERATING PROCEDURES FOR CIVIL CONSTRUCTION NOC ISSUANCE
SUBJECT: Comprehensive Guidelines on Management of Defence Lands, Prohibition of Unauthorized Land Relinquishments by Local Commanders, Kargil War Veterans Housing Scheme Eligibility Protocols, NOC Delegation Rules, and General Land Register Audit Protocols.

1. STATUTORY POLICY ON DEFENCE LAND MANAGEMENT

1.1 Land owned or possessed by the Ministry of Defence constitutes a strategic sovereign asset. Under the statutory provisions of the Cantonments Act and the Defence Land Policy, 1995 (as amended in 2011), no military officer, local commander, General Officer Commanding (GOC), or Defence Estates Officer possesses the legal authority to alienate, transfer, exchange, or relinquish title of defense land to any state government, municipality, or private housing society without explicit approval of the Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS) or the Union Minister of Defence.

1.2 Any No Objection Certificate (NOC) or letter issued by a local military authority attempting to relinquish land ownership or grant construction rights without MoD sanction is void ab initio.

3. POLICY GUIDELINES FOR DEFENCE PERSONNEL WELFARE HOUSING SOCIETIES

3.1 Eligibility Norms for Welfare Housing: Housing schemes sponsored for Army/Navy/Air Force personnel or war widows (e.g., Kargil War Welfare Schemes) must ensure that at least 100% of initial allotment members are serving or retired defense personnel or surviving dependents. Inclusion of civilian politicians, bureaucrats, or non-defense personnel in welfare housing societies formed on or adjacent to defense land is strictly illegal.

4. REVISED GUIDELINES FOLLOWING COLABA / ADARSH LAND CONTROVERSIES

4.1 Re-Verification of Urban Defense Lands (May 2011 Directive): Following irregularities detected in the allotment and NOC issuance for Plot CS No. 652/653 in Colaba, Mumbai, the Ministry of Defence ordered a nationwide audit of all urban defense plots situated near metropolitan coastlines and cantonment borders.

5. ROUTINE CANTONMENT REVENUE & AUDIT INSTRUCTIONS

5.1 Annual Land Audit Protocols: Detailed instructions to DEO officers on maintaining computerized General Land Registers (GLR) and issuing annual physical verification certificates.
